<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 6 and Note 12(c) for additional information on loss reserves. </p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000470" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(l) Earnings Per Share of Common Stock Attributable to Alleghany Stockholders </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic earnings per share of common stock is based on the average number of shares of outstanding common stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000531" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, of Alleghany (&#8220;Common Stock&#8221;) during the period, retroactively adjusted for stock dividends, where applicable. Diluted earnings per share of Common Stock are based on those shares used to calculate basic earnings per share of Common Stock plus the dilutive effect of stock-based compensation awards, retroactively adjusted for stock dividends, where applicable. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 11 for additional information on earnings per share. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000471" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(m) Stock-Based Compensation Plans </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The cost resulting from all stock-based compensation transactions is recognized in the financial statements, with fair value as the measurement objective in accounting for stock-based compensation arrangements. The fair value-based measurement method applies in accounting for stock-based compensation transactions with employees. Non-employee directors are treated as employees for accounting purposes. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 14 for information on Alleghany&#8217;s long-term compensation plans, which include stock-based compensation plans. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000472" name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(n) Senior Notes and Other Debt </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt consists of senior notes issued by Alleghany (the &#8220;Alleghany Senior Notes&#8221;), senior notes issued by TransRe (the &#8220;TransRe Senior Notes,&#8221; and together with the Alleghany Senior Notes, the &#8220;Senior Notes&#8221;) and other debt. Other debt consists primarily of borrowings at Alleghany Capital&#8217;s subsidiaries, and is generally used to fund acquisitions and support working capital needs. The Senior Notes and other debt are carried at unpaid principal balance, including any unamortized premium or discount and any unamortized debt issuance costs. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 8 for additional information on the Senior Notes and other debt. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000473" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionsAndTranslationsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(o) Currency Translation </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are translated into U.S. dollars at period-end exchange rates. Income and expense accounts are translated at average exchange rates for the year. The resulting unrealized currency translation gain or loss for functional currencies is recorded, net of tax, in accumulated other comprehensive income, a component of stockholders&#8217; equity. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transaction gains and losses on assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are recorded as a component of net realized capital gains during the period in which they occur. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000474" name="y:NonInsuranceRevenueAndOtherOperatingExpensesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_befef9f0-085e-4945-bd1f-bf44065eb09b">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(p) Noninsurance Revenue and Other Operating Expenses </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Noninsurance revenues relate primarily to manufactured products and services sold by Alleghany Capital&#8217;s subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Manufactured products primarily include fabricated steel, toys, trailers, machine tools and funeral products. Services primarily include facility design, construction management, technical services and hotel management and development. Noninsurance revenues and related operating expenses arising from the sale of manufactured goods and services are generally recognized as the transfer of goods and services to customers takes place. Payment terms for products and services vary by the type of product or service offered. Noninsurance revenues reflect the payment or payments that are expected to be received from the customers for those goods and services. Other operating expenses consist of the cost of goods and services sold and selling, general and administrative expenses. Other operating expenses also include: (i) advertising and marketing costs&#59; and (ii) finders&#8217; fees, legal and accounting costs and other transaction-related expenses, all of which are recognized as incurred.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Noninsurance revenues and related operating expenses from manufactured products are generally recognized at the time title transfers to the customer, which typically occurs at the point of shipment or delivery to the customer, depending on the terms of the sales arrangement. For certain products, partial payment in the form of a deposit is required before the products are delivered to the customer and such deposits are recorded as a component of other liabilities. For certain manufactured products, </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">141</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000437_dcnt_00075164-8304-4dd4-8a20-42167de63c28" continuedAt="F_000437_dcnt_46f279ba-d6c1-475b-b8af-2cfa1ff735d3"><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_befef9f0-085e-4945-bd1f-bf44065eb09b">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">customers </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">are</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> provide</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">one or more of the following programs: (i) sales incentives&#59; (ii) </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">support </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">for customer promotions&#59;</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(iii) </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">allowances for returns</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> or defective merchandise. Estimates for the cost of these programs are </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">recorded as revenue adjustments that reduce revenue in the period the related sale is recognized.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Noninsurance revenues and related operating expenses from services are generally recognized as the services are performed. Services provided pursuant to a contract are recognized either over the contract period or upon completion of the elements specified in the contract, depending on the terms of the contract. Service revenues related to uncompleted facility construction projects are further recognized as the work progresses, which involve estimates of costs needed to complete the facilities, among other things. The cumulative impact of revisions in total cost estimates are reflected in the period in which these changes become known, including, to the extent required, the increase or reversal of profit recognized in prior periods. External factors, such as weather, changes in customer requirements and other factors outside of Alleghany&#8217;s control, may affect the progress and estimated cost of a project&#8217;s completion and, therefore, the timing and amount of recognition of revenues and income. Provisions for estimated losses on uncompleted contracts, if any, are made in the period in which such losses are determined.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For certain customer contracts in the technical service and hotel management businesses, construction-related costs and recurring hotel operating expenses that Alleghany Capital subsidiaries control and oversee as a principal are incurred and recognized as other operating expenses, but are passed through to the customer and correspondingly recognized as noninsurance revenues. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounts receivable arising from noninsurance revenue are reported as a component of other assets and net of an allowance for credit losses. Such allowance reflects all expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of accounts receivable based on historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. In this regard, amounts outstanding, the current business environment, length of collection periods, the creditworthiness of the customer and other relevant factors are reviewed and considered on an ongoing basis. Amounts deemed to be uncollectible are written off against the allowance. Subsequent reversals in credit loss estimates are permitted and are recognized in earnings.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000475" name="us-gaap:PriorPeriodReclassificationAdjustmentDescription" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(q) Reclassification </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain prior year amounts have been reclassified to conform to the 2020 presentation of the financial statements. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000476" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000476_dcnt_bbab90af-c001-4192-af2d-7dce92e90944">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(r) Recent Accounting Standards </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently Adopted - 2018</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2018, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued guidance on certain tax effects caused by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (the &#8220;Tax Act&#8221;). The Tax Act, among other things, reduced the U.S. corporate federal income tax rate for the 2018 tax year from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000532" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0000775368_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000533" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0000775368_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent. Under such circumstances, GAAP requires that the value of deferred tax assets and liabilities be reduced through tax expense. The new guidance provides an option to reclassify to retained earnings any stranded tax amounts that remain in accumulated other comprehensive income, either retrospectively or at the beginning of the period in which the adoption is elected. This guidance became effective in the first quarter of 2018 for public entities, with early adoption permitted in 2017. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2018 and has elected to reclassify to retained earnings stranded tax amounts that remain in accumulated other comprehensive income, in the amount of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000534" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquity" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRestatementAxis_srtRevisionOfPriorPeriodAccountingStandardsUpdateAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201802Member_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapRetainedEarningsMember_20171231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000535" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquity" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRestatementAxis_srtRevisionOfPriorPeriodAccountingStandardsUpdateAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201802Member_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapAccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeMember_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">135</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, as of January&#160;1, 2018. See Note 10(b) for additional information on accumulated other comprehensive income. See Note 9 for additional information on the Tax Act and its impact on Alleghany.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2016, the FASB issued guidance that changes the recognition and measurement of certain financial instruments. This guidance requires investments in equity securities (except those accounted for under the equity method of accounting, but including partnership investments not accounted for under the equity method) to be measured at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in net earnings. For equity securities that do not have readily determinable fair values, measurement may be at cost, adjusted for any impairment and changes resulting from observable price changes for a similar investment of the same issuer. This guidance also changes the presentation and disclosure of financial instruments by: (i)&#160;requiring that financial instrument disclosures of fair value use the exit price notion&#59; (ii)&#160;requiring separate presentation of financial assets and financial liabilities by measurement category and form, either on the balance sheet or the accompanying notes to the financial statements&#59; (iii)&#160;requiring separate presentation in other comprehensive income for the portion of the change in a liability&#8217;s fair value resulting from instrument-specific credit risk when an election has been made to measure the liability at fair value&#59; and (iv)&#160;eliminating the requirement to disclose the methods and significant assumptions used to estimate the fair value for financial instruments measured at amortized cost on the balance sheet. This guidance became effective for fiscal years beginning after December&#160;15, 2017 for public entities, including interim periods within those fiscal years. Except for the change in presentation for instrument-specific credit risk, this guidance does not permit early adoption. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2018. As of January&#160;1,&#160;2018, approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000536" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquity" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRestatementAxis_srtRevisionOfPriorPeriodAccountingStandardsUpdateAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201601Member_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapRetainedEarningsMember_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000537" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquity" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRestatementAxis_srtRevisionOfPriorPeriodAccountingStandardsUpdateAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201601Member_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapAccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeMember_20171231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">736</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of net unrealized gains of equity securities, net of deferred taxes, were reclassified from accumulated other comprehensive income to retained earnings. Subsequently, all changes in unrealized gains or losses of equity securities, net of deferred taxes, were presented in the Consolidated Statements of Earnings rather than the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income, under the caption &#8220;change in the fair value of equity securities.&#8221; Results arising from partnership investments, whether accounted for under the equity method or at fair value, continue </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">142</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000437_dcnt_46f279ba-d6c1-475b-b8af-2cfa1ff735d3" continuedAt="F_000437_dcnt_cb54d19e-fe12-4b03-abd6-7cebd1277a76"><ix:continuation id="F_000476_dcnt_bbab90af-c001-4192-af2d-7dce92e90944" continuedAt="F_000476_dcnt_dc2c88e0-f0cb-4c3e-91c0-7e0f5bef3423">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">to be reported as a component of net investment income. The implementation did not have a material impact on Alleghany&#8217;s financial condition. See Note 4 for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s equity securities, and Note 10(b) for further information on accumulated other comprehensive income.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2014, the FASB, together with the International Accounting Standards Board, issued guidance on the recognition of revenue from contracts with customers. Under this guidance, revenue is recognized as the transfer of goods and services to customers takes place and in amounts that reflect the payment or payments that are expected to be received from the customers for those goods and services. This guidance also requires new disclosures about revenue. Revenue related to insurance and reinsurance contracts and revenue from investments are not impacted by this guidance, whereas noninsurance revenue arising from the sale of manufactured goods and services is generally included within the scope of this guidance. This guidance, and all related amendments, became effective in the first quarter of 2018 for public entities, with early adoption permitted in 2017. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2018 using the modified retrospective transition approach and the implementation did not have a material impact on Alleghany&#8217;s results of operations and financial condition. See Note 13 for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s noninsurance revenues.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently Adopted - 2019<span style="font-style:normal;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the FASB issued guidance on leases. Under this guidance, a lessee is required to recognize lease liabilities and corresponding right-of-use assets for leases with terms of more than one year, whereas under the prior guidance, a lessee was only required to recognize assets and liabilities for those leases qualifying as capital leases. This guidance also requires new disclosures about the amount, timing and uncertainty of cash flows arising from leases. The accounting by lessors remains largely unchanged. This guidance became effective in the first quarter of 2019 for public companies, with early adoption permitted. A modified retrospective transition approach was elected for all leases in existence as of, or entered into after, the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented in the financial statements. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2019, and the implementation did not have a material impact on its results of operations and financial condition. As part of its implementation, Alleghany elected to not separate lease components from non-lease components (such as office cleanings, security and maintenance services provided by Alleghany&#8217;s lessors for certain of its leases). Alleghany also elected the package of practical expedients under the transition guidance, which allowed Alleghany to not reevaluate existing lease classifications, among others. As of January&#160;1, 2019, Alleghany&#8217;s adoption of this guidance resulted in recognition of an additional right-of-use asset of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000538" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAxis_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and a corresponding lease liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000539" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAxis_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion. See Note 12(b) for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s leases. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2017, the FASB issued guidance that simplifies the requirements to achieve hedge accounting, better reflects the economic results of hedging in financial statements and improves the alignment between hedge accounting and a company&#8217;s risk management activities. This guidance was effective in the first quarter of 2019 for public companies, with early adoption permitted. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2019 and the implementation did not have a material impact on its results of operations and financial condition.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently Adopted &#8211; 2020</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, the FASB issued guidance on credit losses. Under this guidance, a company is required to measure all expected credit losses on loans, reinsurance recoverables and other financial assets accounted for at cost or amortized cost, as applicable, over the remaining expected life of such assets. Estimates of expected credit losses are to be based on historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Under former FASB guidance, credit losses on these assets generally required a company to recognize credit losses when it was probable that a loss had been incurred. Credit losses for securities accounted for on an available for sale (&#8220;AFS&#8221;) basis are to be measured in a manner similar to GAAP as applied under former guidance and cannot exceed the amount by which the fair value is less than the amortized cost, although the new guidance removes the length of time a security has been in an unrealized loss position as a possible indication of a credit impairment. Credit losses for all financial assets are to be recorded through an allowance for credit losses. Subsequent reversals in credit loss estimates are permitted and are to be recognized in earnings. This guidance also requires new disclosures about the significant estimates and judgments used in estimating credit losses, as well as the credit quality of financial assets. This guidance was effective in the first quarter of 2020 for public companies, with early adoption permitted. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2020. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 1, 2020, Alleghany increased its allowances for credit losses on certain financial assets accounted for at cost or amortized cost by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000540" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAxis_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_20200101_20200101" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.5</ix:nonFraction> million and recorded an after-tax cumulative effect reduction in opening retained earnings of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000541" name="us-gaap:RetainedEarningsAccumulatedDeficit" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAxis_srtCumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAdjustmentMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_20200101" decimals="-5" sign="-" scale="6">3.6</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;The increase in allowances for credit losses primarily relates to reinsurance recoverables and commercial mortgage loans. See Note 5 for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance recoverables and Note 4(j) for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s investments in commercial mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;The increase in allowances for credit losses also relates to premium balances receivable.&#160;&#160;Estimates of expected credit losses for all of these assets are based on certain market-based indicators of credit quality, which are updated on an annual basis and re-assessed at least quarterly. Related credit loss expenses are recorded as a component of other operating expenses.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 1, 2020, credit losses for Alleghany&#8217;s AFS securities are recorded through an allowance for credit losses on the consolidated balance sheets and as a change in allowance for credit losses on AFS securities in the consolidated statements of earnings and comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;See Note 4(f) for further information on the credit quality for Alleghany&#8217;s AFS securities. </p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">143</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000437_dcnt_cb54d19e-fe12-4b03-abd6-7cebd1277a76" continuedAt="F_000437_dcnt_cd506b3a-219c-4162-9565-336bd3f58757"><ix:continuation id="F_000476_dcnt_dc2c88e0-f0cb-4c3e-91c0-7e0f5bef3423" continuedAt="F_000476_dcnt_771b268f-c1b0-4011-8b67-967fcd1f6a19">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2017, the FASB issued guidance that simplifies the subsequent measurement of goodwill. Under this guidance, if an initial qualitative assessment indicates that the fair value of an operating subsidiary may be less than its carrying amount, an impairment charge is recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount of the operating subsidiary exceeds its estimated fair value. Any resulting impairment loss recognized cannot exceed the total amount of goodwill associated with the operating subsidiary. This guidance was effective in the first quarter of 2020 for public companies, with early adoption permitted. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2020 and the implementation did not have a material impact on its results of operations and financial condition. See Note 2</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">for further information on Alleghany&#8217;s goodwill. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2018, the FASB issued guidance that changes the financial statement disclosure requirements for measuring fair value. With respect to financial instruments classified as &#8220;Level&#160;3&#8221; in the fair value disclosure hierarchy, the guidance requires certain additional disclosures for public companies related to amounts included in other comprehensive income and significant unobservable inputs used in the valuation, while removing disclosure requirements related to an entity&#8217;s overall valuation processes. The guidance also removes certain disclosure requirements related to transfers between financial instruments classified as &#8220;Level&#160;1&#8221; and &#8220;Level&#160;2&#8221; and provides clarification on certain other existing disclosure requirements. This guidance was effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&#160;15, 2019, with early adoption permitted with respect to any eliminated or modified disclosures. Alleghany adopted this guidance in the first quarter of 2020 and the implementation did not impact its results of operations or financial condition. See Note 3 for further information on the fair value of Alleghany&#8217;s financial instruments. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2020, the FASB issued guidance to expedite and simplify the accounting associated with the anticipated migration away from the widely-used London Inter-bank Offered Rate and other similar rates as benchmark interest rates after 2021.&#160;&#160;Under pre-existing GAAP, such modifications made to: (i) loans and certain other contracts would require re-assessments of the accounting for those contacts, such as whether they were extinguished and remeasured from an accounting perspective&#59; and (ii) derivative contracts may cause a change in accounting, such as a possible dedesignation of hedge accounting. This new guidance largely eliminates these requirements as a result of this migration to one or more new benchmark rates and is generally applicable for contract modifications made prior to December 31, 2022. Alleghany adopted this guidance in March 2020 and the implementation did not have an impact on its results of operations and financial condition.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Future Application of Accounting Standards <span style="font-style:normal;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2020, the FASB issued guidance that simplifies the accounting and disclosure requirements for certain financial instruments with characteristics of liabilities and equity, such as convertible debt and convertible preferred stock. This guidance also modifies the accounting for certain contracts involving an entity&#8217;s own stock. This guidance is effective in the first quarter of 2022 for public companies, with early adoption permitted. Alleghany will adopt this guidance in the first quarter of 2022 and does not currently believe that the implementation will have a material impact on its results of operations and financial condition.</p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">144</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With respect to changes in Level 3 liabilities during 2020, the increase in senior notes and other debt reflects the impact of Wilbert&#8217;s April 1, 2020 inclusion in Alleghany&#8217;s consolidated results, as discussed above and, to a lesser extent, increased borrowings at other Alleghany Capital subsidiaries due to greater working capital needs.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Although Alleghany is responsible for the determination of the fair value of Alleghany&#8217;s financial assets and the supporting methodologies and assumptions, it employs third-party valuation service providers to gather, analyze and interpret market information and derive fair values based upon relevant methodologies and assumptions for individual instruments. When those providers are unable to obtain sufficient market observable information upon which to estimate the fair value for a particular security, fair value is determined either by requesting a quote, which is generally non-binding, from brokers who are knowledgeable about these securities or by employing widely accepted valuation models. As of December 31, 2020 and December 31, 2019, the fair value for the vast majority of debt securities included in Level 3 was provided by such third-party valuation service providers, and as such, valuation details on these securities are generally not available to Alleghany.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany employs specific control processes to determine the reasonableness of the fair values of its financial assets and liabilities. Alleghany&#8217;s processes are designed to ensure that the values received or internally estimated are accurately recorded and that the data inputs and the valuation techniques used are appropriate, consistently applied and that the assumptions are reasonable and consistent with the objective of determining fair value. Alleghany assesses the reasonableness of individual security values received from valuation service providers through various analytical techniques. In addition, Alleghany validates the reasonableness of fair values by comparing information obtained from Alleghany&#8217;s valuation service providers to other third-party valuation sources for selected securities. Alleghany also validates prices obtained from brokers for selected securities through reviews by those who have relevant expertise and who are independent of those charged with executing investing transactions. </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 1(c) for Alleghany&#8217;s accounting policy on fair value. </p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gross realized loss amounts exclude change in allowance for credit losses on AFS securities, as discussed below. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(f) Credit quality for AFS securities </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany holds its debt securities as AFS and, as such, these securities are recorded at fair value. Credit losses for AFS securities are recorded through an allowance for credit losses. Changes in the allowance for credit losses are recorded for (or as a reversal of) credit losses on AFS securities. Any portion of a decline in fair value related to a debt security that is believed to arise from factors other than credit is recorded as a component of other comprehensive income rather than charged against earnings.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001292" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleSecuritiesInUnrealizedLossPositionsQualitativeDisclosureNature" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231"><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany continually monitors the difference between amortized cost and the estimated fair value of its debt investments. The analysis of a security&#8217;s decline in value is performed in its functional currency. Debt securities in an unrealized loss position are evaluated for credit losses if they meet any of the following criteria: (i) they are trading at a discount of at least 20 percent to amortized cost and have a credit rating below investment grade or are not rated&#59; (ii) there has been a negative credit or news event with respect to the issuer that could indicate the existence of a credit loss&#59; or (iii) Alleghany intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that Alleghany will sell, the debt security before recovery of its amortized cost basis. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If Alleghany intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that Alleghany will sell, a debt security before recovery of its amortized cost basis, the total amount of the unrealized loss position is recognized as a credit loss in earnings. To the extent that a debt security that is in an unrealized loss position is not impaired based on the preceding, Alleghany will consider a debt security to be impaired when it believes it to be probable that Alleghany will not be able to collect the entire amortized cost basis. For debt securities in an unrealized loss position as of the end of each quarter, Alleghany develops a best estimate of the present value of expected cash flows. If the results of the cash flow analysis indicate that Alleghany will not recover the full amount of its amortized cost basis in the debt security, Alleghany records a credit loss in earnings equal to the difference between the present value of expected cash flows and the amortized cost basis of the debt security. If applicable, the difference between the total unrealized loss position on the debt security and the total loss recognized in earnings is the non-credit related portion, which is recorded as a component of other comprehensive income.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In developing the cash flow analyses for debt securities, Alleghany considers various factors for the different categories of debt securities. For municipal bonds, Alleghany takes into account the taxing power of the issuer, source of revenue, credit risk and enhancements and pre-refunding. For mortgage and asset-backed securities, Alleghany discounts its best estimate of future cash flows at an effective rate equal to the original effective yield of the security or, in the case of floating rate securities, at the current coupon. Alleghany&#8217;s models include assumptions about prepayment speeds, default and delinquency rates, underlying collateral (if any), credit ratings, credit enhancements and other observable market data. For corporate bonds, Alleghany reviews business prospects, credit ratings and available information from asset managers and rating agencies for individual securities.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Change in allowance for credit losses on AFS securities in 2020 reflect $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001293" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleChangeInPresentValueExpenseReversal" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">8.0</ix:nonFraction> million of unrealized losses on debt securities, primarily related to the energy sector and lower-quality corporate bonds in other sectors due to a significant decline in </p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The gross unrealized investment losses for debt securities as of December 31, 2020 were deemed to be temporary, based on, among other factors: (i)&#160;the relative magnitude to which the fair value of these investments had been below cost were not indicative of a credit loss&#59; (ii)&#160;the absence of compelling evidence that would cause Alleghany to call into question the financial condition or near-term business prospects of the issuer of the security&#59; and (iii)&#160;Alleghany&#8217;s ability and intent to hold the security for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany&#8217;s methodology for assessing credit losses contains inherent risks and uncertainties which could include, but are not limited to, incorrect assumptions about financial condition, liquidity or future prospects, inadequacy of any underlying collateral and unfavorable changes in economic conditions or social trends, interest rates or credit ratings. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany&#8217;s consolidated investment portfolio consists mainly of highly rated and liquid debt and equity securities listed on national securities exchanges. The overall credit quality of the debt securities portfolio is measured using the lowest rating of three large, reputable rating agencies. In this regard, the overall weighted-average credit quality rating of Alleghany&#8217;s debt securities portfolio as of December 31, 2020 and 2019, was AA-. Although a portion of Alleghany&#8217;s debt securities, which consist predominantly of municipal bonds, is insured by third-party financial guaranty insurance companies, the impact of such insurance was not significant to the debt securities&#8217; credit quality rating as of December 31, 2020.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000488" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableCreditQualityIndicatorsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000488_dcnt_42a443ad-2508-4377-b92c-ce5ad1b2609c"></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, Alleghany held a total of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_yInvestment" id="F_001476" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" contextRef="C_0000775368_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_us-gaapDebtSecuritiesMember_20201231" decimals="INF">506</ix:nonFraction> debt securities that were in an unrealized loss position, of which <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_yInvestment" id="F_001477" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleContinuousUnrealizedLossPosition12MonthsOrLongerNumberOfPositions" contextRef="C_0000775368_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_us-gaapDebtSecuritiesMember_20201231" decimals="INF">115</ix:nonFraction> securities were in an unrealized loss position continuously for 12 months or more. The unrealized losses associated with these debt securities consisted of losses related primarily to other asset-backed securities, U.S. corporate bonds and CMBS. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(h) Statutory Deposits </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investments with fair values of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001478" name="y:FairValueOfInvestmentsDepositedWithGovernmentAuthorities" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-8" scale="9">2.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion as of December&#160;31, 2020, the substantial majority of which were debt securities and equity securities, were deposited with governmental authorities as required by law. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(i) Investments in Certain Other Invested Assets </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2012, TransRe obtained an ownership interest in Pillar Capital Holdings Limited (&#8220;Pillar Holdings&#8221;), a Bermuda- based insurance asset manager focused on collateralized reinsurance and catastrophe insurance-linked securities. Additionally, TransRe and, to a lesser extent, AIHL invested in limited partnership funds managed by Pillar Holdings (the &#8220;Funds&#8221;). The objective of the Funds is to create portfolios with attractive risk-reward characteristics and low correlation with other asset classes, using the extensive reinsurance and capital market experience of the principals of Pillar Holdings. Alleghany has concluded that both Pillar Holdings and the Funds (collectively, the &#8220;Pillar Investments&#8221;) represent variable interest entities and that Alleghany is not the primary beneficiary, as it does not have the ability to direct the activities that most significantly impact each entity&#8217;s economic performance. Therefore, the Pillar Investments are not consolidated and are accounted for under the equity method of accounting. Alleghany&#8217;s potential maximum loss in the Pillar Investments is limited to its cumulative net investment. As of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, Alleghany&#8217;s carrying value in the Pillar Investments, as determined under the equity method of accounting, was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001479" name="us-gaap:OtherInvestments" contextRef="C_0000775368_us-gaapInvestmentSecondaryCategorizationAxis_yPillarCapitalHoldingsLimitedAndManagedFundsMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">173.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001480" name="us-gaap:OtherInvestments" contextRef="C_0000775368_us-gaapInvestmentSecondaryCategorizationAxis_yPillarCapitalHoldingsLimitedAndManagedFundsMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">205.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, which is reported as a component of other invested assets and is net of returns of capital received from the Pillar Investments. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(j) Investments in Commercial Mortgage Loans </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, the carrying value of Alleghany&#8217;s commercial mortgage loan portfolio was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001481" name="us-gaap:MortgageLoansOnRealEstateCommercialAndConsumerNet" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">670.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001482" name="us-gaap:MortgageLoansOnRealEstateCommercialAndConsumerNet" contextRef="C_0000775368_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">686.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, representing the unpaid principal balance on the loans, less allowance for credit losses. The estimated fair value of the commercial mortgage loan portfolio approximated carrying value of as December 31, 2020 and 2019. The commercial mortgage loan portfolio consists primarily of first mortgages on commercial properties in major metropolitan areas in the U.S. The loans earn interest at fixed- and floating-rates, and mature in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001483" name="y:CommercialMortgageLoanTermOfLoan" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_04a1c173-0e9e-4fec-b95c-bfc481c9f64b">two</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001484" name="y:CommercialMortgageLoanTermOfLoan" contextRef="C_0000775368_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten<ix:continuation id="C_04a1c173-0e9e-4fec-b95c-bfc481c9f64b"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> from loan origination. As of December 31, 2020, the vast majority of loans in Alleghany&#8217;s portfolio were originated in the 2016 through 2019 years.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> The principal amounts of the loans were no more than approximately two-thirds of the property&#8217;s appraised value at the time the loans were made and the estimated fair value of underlying collateral was approximately double that of the commercial mortgage loan portfolio carrying value as of December 31, 2020.&#160;&#160;Fair value estimates of underlying collateral are updated on a rolling basis at least annually, with a portion of the portfolio updated each quarter. As of December 31, 2020, there was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001485" name="y:CommercialMortgageLoansInDefaultOrInArrears" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction> loan in default or in arrears. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000490" name="y:CommercialMortgageLoanAllowanceForCreditLossTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000490_dcnt_fe52d50b-7ec7-4489-ad02-36fa3d06bb14"></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5<span style="font-style:italic;">.</span> Reinsurance Ceded </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(a) Overview </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries reinsure portions of the risks they underwrite in order to reduce the effect of individual or aggregate exposure to losses, manage capacity, protect capital resources, reduce volatility in specific lines of business, improve risk-adjusted portfolio returns and enable them to increase gross premium writings and risk capacity without requiring additional capital. Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries generally purchase reinsurance and retrocessional coverages from highly-rated third-party reinsurers or on a collateralized basis. If the assuming reinsurers are unable or unwilling to meet the obligations assumed under the applicable reinsurance agreements, Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries would remain liable for such reinsurance portion not paid by these reinsurers. As such, funds, trust agreements and letters of credit are held to collateralize a portion of Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance recoverables and Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries reinsure portions of the risks they underwrite or assume with multiple reinsurance programs. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(b) Reinsurance Recoverables </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000491" name="y:ReinsuranceInformationTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

Such balances as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 are presented in the table below: </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(d) Significant Reinsurance Contracts </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries reinsure portions of the risks they underwrite or assume with multiple reinsurance programs. A summary of the more significant programs follows. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">TransRe enters into various retrocession arrangements, including property catastrophe retrocession contracts, to manage the effects of individual or aggregate exposure to losses, reduce volatility in specific lines of business, improve risk-adjusted portfolio returns, strengthen its market position and enhance capital efficiency. These include excess-of-loss and quota share treaties in both traditional rated and collateralized form as well as catastrophe bonds. TransRe&#8217;s retrocession protections generally have a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001564">one-year</span> term and renewal dates occur throughout the year, with the majority renewing at January 1. The catastrophe bonds, however, have a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001565">four-year</span> term, with maturities in 2022 and 2023.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RSUI reinsures its property lines of business through a program consisting of surplus share treaties, facultative placements, and per risk and catastrophe excess of loss treaties. RSUI&#8217;s catastrophe reinsurance program and property per risk reinsurance program each run on an annual basis from May&#160;1 to the following April&#160;30 and portions expired on April&#160;30, 2020. Both programs were renewed on May&#160;1, 2020 with substantially similar terms as the expired programs. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.67%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(e) Significant AIHL Re Reinsurance Contracts </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AIHL Re and CapSpecialty entered into an intercompany reinsurance contract, effective July&#160;1, 2015, pursuant to which AIHL Re provides CapSpecialty with coverage primarily for adverse development on certain net loss and allocated LAE in excess of its carried reserves at June&#160;30, 2015. AIHL Re&#8217;s commitments are intended to cover the statutory collateral requirements at CapSpecialty, if and when necessary, and AIHL Re&#8217;s obligations are subject to an aggregate limit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001566" name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_us-gaapFinancialGuaranteeMember_us-gaapReinsurancePolicyTypeAxis_yAihlReLimitedLiabilityCompanyReinsuranceOfCapSpecialtyIncorporatedMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">50.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. In connection with such intercompany reinsurance agreement, Alleghany and AIHL Re entered into a contract whereby Alleghany will guarantee the recoverable balances owed to CapSpecialty from AIHL Re up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001567" name="y:ReinsuranceCoverage" contextRef="C_0000775368_us-gaapReinsurancePolicyTypeAxis_yAihlReLimitedLiabilityCompanyReinsuranceOfCapSpecialtyIncorporatedMember_us-gaapSubsegmentsAxis_yCapSpecialtyIncorporatedMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">50.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The above agreements had no impact on Alleghany&#8217;s consolidated results of operations and financial condition. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the December 31, 2017 sale of Pacific Compensation Corporation (&#8220;PacificComp&#8221;) by AIHL, AIHL Re provides adverse development reinsurance coverage to the acquirer on PacificComp&#8217;s pre-acquisition claims, subject to certain terms and conditions. AIHL Re&#8217;s obligation, which are guaranteed by Alleghany, are subject to an aggregate limit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001568" name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_us-gaapFinancialGuaranteeMember_us-gaapReinsurancePolicyTypeAxis_yAihlReLimitedLiabilityCompanyReinsuranceOfPacificCompensationInsuranceCompanyMember_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">150.0</ix:nonFraction> million and a final commutation and settlement as of December 31, 2024.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">159</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">7. Credit Agreements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_002547" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityInitiationDate1" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20170731_20170731" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">July&#160;31, 2017</ix:nonNumeric>, Alleghany entered into a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_002548">five-year</span> credit agreement (the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;) with certain lenders party thereto, which provides for an unsecured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002549" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20170731" decimals="INF" scale="6">300.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The credit facility is scheduled to expire on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_002550" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20170731_20170731" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">July&#160;31, 2022</ix:nonNumeric>, unless earlier terminated. Borrowings under the Credit Agreement will be available for working capital and general corporate purposes, including permitted acquisitions and repurchases of Common Stock. Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear a floating rate of interest based in part on Alleghany&#8217;s credit rating, among other factors. The Credit Agreement contains representations, warranties and covenants customary for bank loan facilities of this nature. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002551" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002552" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002553" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> borrowings under the Credit Agreement in 2020, 2019 and 2018 and there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002554" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityFairValueOfAmountOutstanding" contextRef="C_0000775368_deiLegalEntityAxis_yAlleghanyCorporationMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction> outstanding borrowings under the Credit Agreement as of December&#160;31, 2020. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(1) <ix:footnote id="FNT_000051" xml:lang="en-US">For 2020, includes various general business credits and tax benefits resulting from corporate acquisitions and dispositions, partially offset by disallowed expense deductions primarily related to certain executive compensation paid in 2020.</ix:footnote></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate in 2020 primarily reflects modest pre-tax income and the resulting increase of the impact from permanent tax benefits, such as tax-exempt interest income and dividends-received deductions, when expressed on an effective tax rate basis. The higher effective tax rate in 2019 primarily reflects significant pre-tax earnings and the resulting decrease from the impact of these permanent tax benefits when expressed on an effective tax rate basis.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The increase in effective tax rate in 2019 compared with 2018 primarily reflects the impact of higher earnings before income taxes and, to a lesser extent, lower tax-exempt interest income arising from municipal bond securities and lower dividends-received deductions, partially offset by higher state income taxes. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security Act (the &#8220;CARES Act&#8221;) was signed into law on March 27, 2020.&#160;&#160;Among other provisions, the CARES Act delayed certain employer payroll tax remittance deadlines and created or expanded certain income tax credits and loss carryback provisions.<span style="font-size:12pt;"> </span>The beneficial impact of the CARES Act to Alleghany is currently not material.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000507" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfDeferredTaxAssetsAndLiabilitiesTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.67%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(c) Regulations and Dividend Restrictions </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002794" name="y:StockholdersEquityUnavailableForDividendsOrAdvances" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-8" scale="9">7.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion of Alleghany&#8217;s total equity of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002795" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquity" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion was unavailable for dividends or advances to Alleghany from its subsidiaries. The remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002796" name="y:StockholdersEquityUnappropriated" contextRef="C_0000775368_20201231" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion was available for dividends or advances to Alleghany from its subsidiaries, or was retained at the Alleghany parent company-level and, as such, was available to pay dividends to Alleghany&#8217;s stockholders as of December&#160;31, 2020.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The ability of Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries to pay dividends or other distributions is subject to the laws and regulations applicable to each subsidiary, as well as each subsidiary&#8217;s need to maintain capital requirements adequate to maintain its operations and financial strength ratings issued by independent rating agencies. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the U.S., Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries are subject to insurance laws and regulations that restrict the amount and timing of dividends they may pay without the prior approval of regulatory authorities. Under the insurance holding company laws and regulations, Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries may not pay an &#8220;extraordinary&#8221; </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">173</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000446_dcnt_b403d7e8-51bc-42c0-aeb9-d9e3f0f510cf" continuedAt="F_000446_dcnt_39b634f4-d0b5-4280-bab3-a4046d4c1705">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">dividend or distribution without the approval of state insurance regulators. In general, an &#8220;extraordinary&#8221; dividend or distribution is defined as a dividend or distribution that, together with other dividends and distributions made within the preceding 12 months, exceeds the lesser (or, in some jurisdictions, the greater) of (i) 10&#160;percent of the statutory surplus of the reinsurer or insurer as of the end of the prior calendar year (or, in certain states, as of the end of the prior quarter) and (ii)&#160;the net income during the prior calendar year (or, in certain states, the adjusted statutory net investment income). In addition, certain states where Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries are domiciled prohibit a domestic insurance company from paying dividends except out of earned surplus. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">TransRe&#8217;s operations are also regulated in various foreign jurisdictions with respect to currency, amount and type of security deposits, amount and type of reserves and amount and type of local investment. Regulations governing constitution of technical reserves and remittance balances in some countries may hinder remittance of profits and repatriation of assets. International operations and assets held abroad may also be adversely affected by political and other developments in foreign countries, including possible tax changes, nationalization and changes in regulatory policy, as well as by consequences of hostilities and unrest. The risks of such occurrences and their overall effect upon TransRe vary from country to country and cannot easily be predicted. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000512" name="us-gaap:DividendsDeclaredTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000775368_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

Aside from Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries, dividends are regularly paid to Alleghany from the subsidiaries of Alleghany Capital, where there are generally no regulatory restrictions on dividends being paid from retained earnings.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.73%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Aside from Alleghany&#8217;s reinsurance and insurance subsidiaries, Alleghany Capital&#8217;s subsidiaries pay dividends to Alleghany Capital based primarily on each subsidiary&#8217;s need to maintain its operations.
